description: Meewasin Valley Authority plants native species to combat climate change.
City and MVA collaborate on climate mitigation and watershed health.
City offers water conservation programs and rain barrel rebates.

chips.text: Received as information
Director of Sustainability discussed integrating Indigenous land use into public spaces.
Rural landowners receive shelterbelt plants from Shand Nurseries.
Meewasin bylaw prohibiting picking wild plants is under review.
MVA replaces lost vegetation at a three-to-one ratio.
City will provide more information on water conservation communication campaigns.

speakers.name: Alan Otterbein
speakers.summary: Alan Otterbein, Meewasin Valley Authority presented on design and landscape development, highlighting the use of native plants to combat climate change and urban heat effects.
said: The planting program supports MVA's conservation and development mandates.
They use native plants, in-house production, and volunteers for restoration and biomass replacement.
Planting improves water quality, mitigates heat, and adapts to climate change.

description: City held climate adaptation workshop for stakeholders.
Public survey, open house planned for broader input.
Committee requested notice for upcoming public open house.

chips.text: Received as information
Discussion on inviting diverse opinions and ensuring respectful public engagement.
Stakeholders included health authority, housing, and environmental groups.
Open house format still being planned to ensure safety of staff and participants.
Workshop focused on climate adaptation, carbon emissions, and green spaces.
Committee will receive prior warning about the upcoming public open house.

description: Saskatchewan rolled back residential energy code to Tier 1.
City will consider options for Tier 1 versus Tier 2.
Report on energy code changes goes to committee May 7, 2025.

chips.text: Received as information
Residential builders and future homeowners are affected by energy code changes.
Unclear if administration's recommendation on energy code requires full council approval.
Builders had mixed feedback, but most preferred city adhere to Tier 2 energy code.
Concerns raised that lower Tier 1 standards could lead to higher long-term energy use.

description: Subcommittee plans social media and campus outreach for Welcome Week.
Discussed incorporating Indigenous land use into programming.

chips.text: University of Saskatchewan students will be targeted for Welcome Week outreach.
Staff clarified that advisory committees do not directly direct administration's work.
Rain barrel rebates can be up to $100 for low-income residents.
